title: Subset sum I: zeroing the remaining target and index-order pruning
summary: Starting from target 9, subtract candidates level by level while combining start = i with a break when a candidate exceeds the remaining target to output [3, 3, 3] and [4, 5].
context: The input consists of the sorted positive integer array choices = [3, 4, 5] (indices 0, 1, 2) and initial target = 9; elements may be chosen repeatedly, and combinations ignore order. The number inside each circular node shows the remaining target balance (9 minus the current prefix sum), reaching a valid subset when reduced to 0.
description: Upon entering a call, if the remaining target is 0, record the current combination and return to the parent call so its loop can continue; otherwise iterate through candidates choices[i] starting from index start, subtract the chosen value from the remaining target, and recurse to the next level. Passing start = i downward allows choosing the current element again while skipping earlier indices (the index-order pruning marked by black scissors in the figure).

Because the candidates are sorted in ascending order, within i ≥ start, encountering the first candidate greater than the remaining target triggers an immediate break after comparison, ending the current loop; neither that candidate nor any larger ones after it are entered recursively. Red scissors in the figure mark these out-of-range branches.

The figure contains 10 circular nodes with nonnegative remaining targets. The table below lists by prefix the remaining target, the restrictions shown in the figure, and the actual continuation; the remaining target 1 under [4, 4] is left unexpanded in the figure, and its subsequent break is supplied from the code rules.

frames.title: Subset sum I: zeroing the remaining target and index-order pruning
frames.explanation: The two paths that reduce the remaining target to 0 are 9 → 6 → 3 → 0 and 9 → 5 → 0, yielding [3, 3, 3] and [4, 5], respectively.
